data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A lease-based protocol augmented with monotonic deterministic epochs and non-replayable tombstones can achieve equivalent safety to log-based protocols while providing superior reclamation latency, adjudicating the rivalry by showing that leases are unsafe only when they lack lineage awareness.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Epoch counters wrap or reset due to storage corruption","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Tombstones are subject to the same crash-asymmetry as evidence and may disappear","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Reconciliation protocol itself can silently displace if it lacks a content-addressed compare","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Deterministic workspace IDs allow pre-computation of future epochs by a faulty process","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The workspace is tagged with a monotonic epoch nonce derived from a durable epoch ledger. Completed evidence is recorded as (problem_id, epoch, content_hash, tombstone_flag). Reclamation increments the epoch and writes a tombstone; any restarted process detects an epoch mismatch and must reconcile before overwriting. The durable record must contain: (1) the current epoch for the problem ID, (2) the content-addressed evidence hash bound to that epoch, and (3) the tombstone record proving reclamation occurred. This adjudicates lease vs log by demonstrating that the lease's flaw\u2014false-positive displacement\u2014is remedied by epoch lineage, not by abandoning leases.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
